name: managed-remote-access-threat-cases
description: Hostile threat matrix for the managed remote-access lane (merge unit A, TASK-5771). Positive controls plus tenant-A-vs-B hostile negatives. Every case carries a stable deny/failure category, a stable audit category, and redacted tenant-neutral failure prose with no raw exception text and no credential material. Paired cases (existence_pair) prove the no-cross-tenant-existence-oracle rule: identical categories whether the target exists or not. All credential inputs are obvious non-secret placeholders.

cases.scenario: A client proof is presented outside its validity window.

expected.failure_detail: Connection denied; the presented proof is outside its validity window.
expected.proves: expired proofs are denied

cases.scenario: A previously used proof/nonce is replayed.

expected.failure_detail: Connection denied; the presented proof was already used or is out of order.
expected.proves: replayed proofs are denied

cases.scenario: A single-use enrollment/pairing credential is presented a second time.

expected.failure_detail: Credential already consumed; reuse rejected.
expected.proves: single-use credentials cannot be reused

cases.scenario: A proof whose audience does not include this connector/home is presented.

expected.failure_detail: Connection denied; the presented proof is not valid for this audience.
expected.proves: wrong-audience credentials are denied

cases.scenario: A credential bound to a different home is presented to this home's connector.

expected.failure_detail: Connection denied; the presented credential is not bound to this home.
expected.proves: home-bound credentials never authorize a different home

cases.scenario: Tenant A's one-use enrollment credential is presented to tenant B's cell enrollment endpoint.

expected.failure_detail: Enrollment denied at the boundary; no confirmation of whether the referenced cell or home exists.
expected.proves: one-use enrollment credentials are cell-bound and single-cell redeemable

cases.scenario: Tenant A's pre-auth key is redeemed at tenant B's cell; redemption is rejected and the credential is consumed/revoked.

expected.failure_detail: Redemption rejected for the presented binding; the attempt is treated as an unknown enrollment.
expected.proves: wrong-cell redemption cannot enroll a node into another cell

cases.scenario: A node identity enrolled in tenant A is reused to join tenant B; B's cell rejects the foreign node identity.

expected.failure_detail: Registration rejected: the presented node identity is not recognized in this cell.
expected.proves: node identities never cross cell boundaries

cases.scenario: Tenant A's device/network key material is presented to tenant B's cell during enrollment.

expected.failure_detail: Enrollment rejected: the presented key is not bound to this cell.
expected.proves: device keys are cell-bound and never reusable across cells

cases.scenario: Tenant A's account session token is used to request enrollment for a home owned by tenant B.

expected.failure_detail: Enrollment request rejected for the referenced home; no confirmation of whether the home exists.
expected.proves: account authority is tenant-scoped; entitlement cannot cross tenants

cases.scenario: Tenant A's account session token is used to request enrollment for a home_id that does not exist anywhere. The response must be indistinguishable from the case where the home exists but belongs to tenant B.

expected.failure_detail: Enrollment request rejected for the referenced home; no confirmation of whether the home exists.
expected.proves: account authority is tenant-scoped; entitlement cannot cross tenants

cases.scenario: Tenant A's credential names a home_id that belongs to tenant B.

expected.failure_detail: Pairing rejected for the referenced home; the home is not resolvable under this tenant.
expected.proves: home identity is tenant-scoped and never resolvable cross-tenant

cases.scenario: A device_id enrolled in tenant A is presented as a current device to a tenant B home connector.

expected.failure_detail: Connection rejected: the presented device is not paired with this home.
expected.proves: device identity is cell-bound and current-device checks are tenant-scoped

cases.scenario: Tenant A node's map request never returns tenant B peers; B's connector port is unreachable from A.

expected.failure_detail: Peer map request denied; no peer data outside the requesting cell is provided.
expected.proves: cross-cell peer data is never disclosed

cases.scenario: Tenant A's map stream omits tenant B entirely; no B endpoint or key data is present.

expected.failure_detail: Map response contains no entries outside the requesting cell.
expected.proves: cell isolation means map data never crosses cells

cases.scenario: Tenant A attempts a direct WireGuard path to tenant B's connector port; the path is denied at the cell boundary.

expected.failure_detail: Direct path denied; no route to the referenced peer exists.
expected.proves: direct WireGuard path never crosses cells

cases.scenario: Tenant A is forced through a DERP relay in an attempt to reach tenant B's connector; relay admission denies the session.

expected.failure_detail: Relay session denied; the relay only serves ciphertext for cells that authorize it.
expected.proves: forced-DERP cannot create cross-cell reachability

cases.scenario: An attacker tries to use the shared DERP fleet to bypass Headscale/cell policy and reach a home the policy denies.

expected.failure_detail: Relay path denied; the relay observes and relays ciphertext only and grants no reachability beyond cell policy.
expected.proves: DERP is a ciphertext relay, never an authorization bypass

cases.scenario: Tenant A client asserts tenant B's tag to gain authority; the policy compiler rejects the tag as not owned.

expected.failure_detail: Tag assertion rejected; tags are compiler output and are never client-asserted authority.
expected.proves: tags cannot be forged across cells

cases.scenario: Tenant A advertises a route that would expose tenant B's subnet; the advertisement is quarantined and denied.

expected.failure_detail: Route advertisement rejected and quarantined; advertised routes are never auto-approved.
expected.proves: route advertisements cannot cross cell boundaries

cases.scenario: Tenant A announces subnet routes into tenant B's address space; announcement is denied.

expected.failure_detail: Subnet advertisement rejected; no route outside the requesting cell is accepted.
expected.proves: subnet advertisements are cell-local only

cases.scenario: Tenant A marks a node as exit node to reach tenant B networks; exit-node use is denied for this product.

expected.failure_detail: Exit-node request denied; exit-node capability is not granted for this product.
expected.proves: exit-node advertisements are always denied

cases.scenario: Tenant A advertises SSH access into tenant B; SSH capability is denied for this product.

expected.failure_detail: SSH request denied; SSH capability is not granted for this product.
expected.proves: SSH advertisements are always denied

cases.scenario: A request arrives from a device that is not the currently paired/current device for this home.

expected.failure_detail: Connection denied; the presented device is not the current paired device for this home.
expected.proves: stale device identity is rejected

cases.scenario: A request arrives with pairing authorization bound to a different home or device.

expected.failure_detail: Connection denied; the pairing authorization does not cover this home/device pair.
expected.proves: pairing authorization is (tenant, home, device)-bound

cases.scenario: An internal connector failure occurs mid-validation.

expected.failure_detail: Request denied; an internal failure occurred and was redacted to category.
expected.proves: internal failures are redacted to category and deny closed

cases.scenario: A request carries bearer-shaped material in remote input (headers, path, or body).

expected.failure_detail: Request rejected; credential-shaped material is never accepted in remote input.
expected.proves: the daemon bearer never appears in remote input

cases.scenario: The local daemon is unreachable or its token file is missing when the connector is ready to forward.

expected.failure_detail: Local daemon unavailable; the connector fails closed and serves no requests.
expected.proves: daemon unavailability fails closed

cases.scenario: The daemon bind is not loopback; the connector refuses to forward.

expected.failure_detail: Forwarding refused; the daemon must remain loopback-bound.
expected.proves: the daemon stays loopback-only; bind mismatch fails closed

cases.scenario: A percent-encoded traversal (..) path is presented; strict decoding reveals the escape and the request is denied.

expected.failure_detail: Path normalization rejected; the decoded path escapes the allowed surface.
expected.proves: percent-encoded traversal is denied

cases.scenario: A dot-dot traversal path is presented.

expected.failure_detail: Path normalization rejected; dot-segment resolution escapes the allowed surface.
expected.proves: dot-segment traversal is denied

cases.scenario: An absolute-form request target (scheme://authority/path) is presented.

expected.failure_detail: Request target rejected; absolute-form/authority ambiguity is denied.
expected.proves: absolute-form request targets are denied

cases.scenario: Empty policy loaded on connector start. The connector must fail closed and deny every request.

expected.failure_detail: Policy state is empty; the connector fails closed and refuses all requests.
expected.proves: missing/malformed/stale/future/rollback policy and compiler/apply failure always fail closed

cases.scenario: Malformed policy artifact (bad signature or schema). The connector must fail closed and deny every request.

expected.failure_detail: Policy artifact is malformed or its signature is invalid; the connector fails closed.
expected.proves: missing/malformed/stale/future/rollback policy and compiler/apply failure always fail closed

cases.scenario: Revocation epoch is behind the required current epoch. The connector must fail closed and deny every request.

expected.failure_detail: Policy/revocation epoch is stale; the connector fails closed.
expected.proves: missing/malformed/stale/future/rollback policy and compiler/apply failure always fail closed

cases.scenario: Policy artifact carries an epoch ahead of the accepted window. The connector must fail closed and deny every request.

expected.failure_detail: Policy/revocation epoch is outside the accepted window; the connector fails closed.
expected.proves: missing/malformed/stale/future/rollback policy and compiler/apply failure always fail closed

cases.scenario: A replayed old policy would decrease the current epoch. The connector must fail closed and deny every request.

expected.failure_detail: Policy/revocation epoch decreased; rollback rejected and the connector fails closed.
expected.proves: missing/malformed/stale/future/rollback policy and compiler/apply failure always fail closed

cases.scenario: Cell policy compiler fails to produce a deny-default artifact. The connector must fail closed and deny every request.

expected.failure_detail: Policy compilation failed; no traffic is authorized until a valid policy is compiled.
expected.proves: missing/malformed/stale/future/rollback policy and compiler/apply failure always fail closed

cases.scenario: Cell policy apply step fails on the connector. The connector must fail closed and deny every request.

expected.failure_detail: Policy apply failed; the connector fails closed and authorizes nothing.
expected.proves: missing/malformed/stale/future/rollback policy and compiler/apply failure always fail closed

cases.scenario: Authenticated, currently paired device with current policy requests an allowed HTTP read route via direct path; connector forwards to loopback daemon.

expected.failure_detail: Request authenticated, binding verified, proof current, policy current, route allowed; forwarded to the loopback daemon with the locally read bearer injected only on the final hop.
expected.proves: fully validated allowed request reaches the loopback daemon

cases.scenario: Authenticated, paired device reads an allowed org task-list route over the direct path.

expected.failure_detail: Allowed read route matched the explicit allow-list template and was forwarded to the loopback daemon.
expected.proves: template allow-list matching authorizes normal browser-consumed reads

cases.scenario: Paired device opens an allowed SSE stream (thread tail); connector validates the GET upgrade and streams events from the loopback daemon.

expected.failure_detail: Allowed SSE upgrade matched an explicitly allowed template; stream established through the relay and served from the loopback daemon.
expected.proves: allowed SSE upgrade semantics work over the relay path

cases.scenario: The device was revoked before presenting a request; revocation epoch is already current.

expected.failure_detail: Connection denied; the device authorization is revoked.
expected.proves: revoked devices are denied before any request is authorized

cases.scenario: Revocation lands while an HTTP request is in flight; the connector closes the stream before completing it.

expected.failure_detail: Stream closed on revocation; no further bytes are served.
expected.proves: revocation closes live HTTP streams immediately

cases.scenario: Revocation lands while an SSE/WebSocket stream is open; the stream is closed and the connector denies subsequent frames.

expected.failure_detail: Stream closed on revocation; subsequent frames are refused.
expected.proves: revocation cancels open SSE/WebSocket streams immediately

cases.scenario: A request targets a forbidden class route (agent completion callback).

expected.failure_detail: Route denied; the normalized target is a forbidden class and never on the allow-list.
expected.proves: agent-callback routes are never remotely reachable

cases.scenario: A mutating method is attempted on a read-only allowed route.

expected.failure_detail: Method denied; the method is not allowed for this surface.
expected.proves: method-awareness: only explicitly allowed methods pass

cases.scenario: A new or unknown route that is not on the allow-list is requested.

expected.failure_detail: Route denied; the route is not on the explicit allow-list.
expected.proves: unclassified and future routes are denied by default

cases.scenario: Conflicting Content-Length / Transfer-Encoding framing (request smuggling) is attempted.

expected.failure_detail: Framing rejected; conflicting body-framing headers are denied.
expected.proves: request smuggling is rejected

cases.scenario: Duplicate critical headers (e.g. repeated Host or Content-Length) are presented.

expected.failure_detail: Headers rejected; duplicate critical headers are denied.
expected.proves: duplicate critical headers are rejected

cases.scenario: One client attempts to reach another client's node; only the paired home connector port is granted.

expected.failure_detail: Connection denied; only the paired home connector surface is granted.
expected.proves: client-to-client traffic is denied

cases.scenario: A home connector attempts an outbound connection to a client node; the reverse direction is denied.

expected.failure_detail: Connection denied; home-to-client connections are not granted.
expected.proves: home-to-client traffic is denied

cases.scenario: An attacker attempts to reach a non-connector port on the home host through the tailnet.

expected.failure_detail: Connection denied; only the connector port is reachable through the network.
expected.proves: non-connector ports are never reachable

cases.scenario: An upgrade to an unsupported protocol is attempted.

expected.failure_detail: Upgrade denied; only explicitly allowed upgrade semantics are supported.
expected.proves: unsupported upgrades are denied

cases.scenario: A body is attached to a surface that forbids bodies.

expected.failure_detail: Request denied; bodies are not permitted on this surface.
expected.proves: unsupported bodies are denied
